extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists entering NPPA Best of Photojournalism; competition entrants, judges, editors
extracted.subtask_description: Judging and entry criteria for the NPPA Best of Photojournalism competition, combining journalistic significance, technical execution, composition, and ethical/visual integrity. Used by entrants to prepare submissions and by judges to evaluate work across listed categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized as a primary consideration – judges look for storytelling ability and the news significance of the work. This is flagged as a key factor in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical excellence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical quality such as correct exposure, sharp focus, and overall image clarity; technical flaws can detract from journalistic effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess visual organization within the frame, use of framing, balance, leading lines, and how compositional choices support storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards (Visual Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPPA Code of Ethics requires: 'Be accurate and comprehensive in the representation of subjects'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two areas of accuracy are highlighted: making the image (no staging) and post-production (no manipulation). Entrants must avoid staging scenes and must not manipulate images in ways that misrepresent events.

rubrics_metrics.name: No staging / accuracy in image capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in the making of the image — no staging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should be authentic captures of events and situations; staged or posed scenes that misrepresent reality violate the ethical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: No manipulation / accuracy in post-production
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-processing must not alter the factual content of images; manipulations that change meaning, add/remove subjects, or mislead are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stories that are relevant to their communities"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work addressing issues, events, or stories that matter to the photographer's community; local resonance is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helps understanding trends and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Help understanding trends and issues for informed decision-making
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should illuminate broader trends or issues to help audiences comprehend their significance and support informed civic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bringing communities together
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photography that fosters community connection or shared understanding is considered valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeply researched photographic enterprise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate thorough reporting and photographic enterprise — reporting depth and effort behind the work matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illuminate and resonate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should both reveal important information and emotionally or intellectually resonate with viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual storytelling power
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual storytelling power — moment, gesture, emotion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for moments, gestures, and emotions that convey narrative and meaning; the capacity of an image to tell a story visually is crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive moment capture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capturing a decisive, newsworthy instant that conveys action or significance strengthens an entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / lack of manipulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces ethical standard: images must truthfully represent events without deceptive alteration; overlaps with both capture and post-production accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject dignity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs should respect the dignity of subjects, avoiding exploitative or dehumanizing portrayals even when documenting difficult circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness of subject matter — same news values apply visually
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional news values (timeliness, impact, prominence, proximity, conflict, human interest, etc.) apply to visual work and are considered in judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: List of entry categories (News Picture Story; Photographer of the Year; Documentary; Sports; Feature Picture; Spot News; General News; Portrait / Personality; Editorial Illustration; Multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants choose the appropriate category for their work; category definitions and expectations inform how judges evaluate submissions within each specialized area.
